description: One open pull request at a time. Every update touches the POM of every blueprint, because the versions are repeated on purpose, so the matrix builds all of them for each one. Four at once occupy the twenty concurrent jobs a free plan gets and leave nothing for the branch somebody is working on. Serialized they cost the same runner time in total and block nobody.

The window is every night between ten in the evening and six in the morning, weekends included. It used to be a Monday morning, and one pull request at a time inside a weekly window means one update a week at best: Renovate picks its own moment to look at a repository, and a look which lands outside those seven hours costs another week on top. Nightly the same queue drains a night per update, and the framework versions a reader copies out of a blueprint stay close to what they would pick themselves.
Merging keeps no window of its own. The matrix builds every blueprint for every update and takes its time, so a pull request opened at three merges whenever it turns green, breakfast included.

'minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour' is loosened because the strict default blocks silently. A release whose datasource reports no publication date can never become three days old, so Renovate parks it as pending and lists it on the dashboard under a heading which reads like a build is running.

packageRules.description: VanillaBP and the BPMS adapters follow the framework, not Renovate. Their versions are bumped when a release is cut, and while they are snapshots there is nothing to look up. Once the adapters are released the Camunda 8 preset extended above takes over, and it keeps a blueprint inside the release line it was written for: the version suffix (2.1.0-8.9) is the lowest cluster version the adapter accepts, and Renovate never proposes an update that changes it.

One pull request for everything Maven, minor and patch. The same version is repeated in every blueprint POM on purpose, so an upgrade touches all of them at once and the matrix builds every blueprint for it. Per dependency that was one full run each; grouped it is one run for all of them, and the property that matters is kept: no blueprint stays behind on a version its neighbour already moved.
Majors stay one pull request per dependency. A green build proves the least there, so they are read rather than counted, and grouping them would hide which one broke what.

The WRAPPER is bumped by hand, the Maven distribution is not. Both live in this manager: 'maven-wrapper' names the wrapper, whose bump requires running the wrapper plugin to rewrite 'mvnw' and 'mvnw.cmd' - the hosted Renovate app cannot do that, its artifact update fails, and what is left replaces version strings while the scripts keep the old logic. 'maven' names the distribution in 'distributionUrl' and is a single line, so those updates work and stay automatic.

The coordinates of the module-packaging blueprint are invented on purpose: it shows an application built from artifacts of its own, and 'com.acme' exists nowhere. Renovate reported them as dependencies it could not look up, which is true and useless, and a permanent warning on the dependency dashboard hides the real ones.

Spring Boot and Quarkus are proposed as a patch and as a minor separately, rather than only as the newest version there is. Without this a waiting minor would hide the patch below it, and the patch is the one which merges itself.

A minor of Spring Boot or Quarkus moves the line the blueprints are written for, and the versions table of CONTRIBUTING.md names that line, so it has to be carried there by hand. It leaves the group above and gets a pull request per platform, because a group is only as fast as the slowest thing in it and this one waits for a person.
